subject.title: [Feature]: /learn command — distill recent work into a reviewable skill draft

question: Should OpenClaw core own `/learn` as a built-in Skill Workshop command, or should this remain a ClawHub/plugin command built on existing command and workshop APIs?
rationale: Current main has the needed Skill Workshop proposal boundary and plugin command seams, while VISION.md both prioritizes ergonomics and cautions against optional core surface area; the protected `maintainer` label means automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Add core `/learn`
options.body: Implement a built-in command that turns optional arguments or current-session context into a guided agent turn that must end in one pending Skill Workshop proposal.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Keep core unchanged and publish a command plugin or bundle that registers `/learn` and invokes the existing Skill Workshop flow through supported APIs.

options.title: Defer until workshop UX settles
options.body: Leave this issue open as a design placeholder until maintainers decide how skill authoring, auto-capture, and command ergonomics should converge.

recommendation.title: Add core `/learn`
recommendation.body: Implement a built-in command that turns optional arguments or current-session context into a guided agent turn that must end in one pending Skill Workshop proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the issue, current blame shows recent work on the implicated command/workshop surfaces, and the item carries the protected maintainer label.
